soundcheck.heard: Alaska has spent decades mapping the days you must not burn. Nobody has mapped the days you can. On July 31, the National Science Foundation paid the University of Alaska Fairbanks $1.6 million to find them. A prescribed burn is a fire you set on purpose, so a wildfire has less to eat. It works, and Alaska barely uses it. NSF says Alaska lacks the forecasting tools, so the Fairbanks team is reading decades of weather with machine learning, hunting for the days that were safe. That isn't a forecast, it's a count of safe days, and a count is something you can hand to people who don't agree. Because land around one village can answer to four governments at once, four parties who've never had the same sheet of paper. So the grant pays to get those four talking, but it isn't finished. None of this reaches a fire proof until 2030, and who pays when a fire escapes isn't in this award. But nothing moves without that count. You can't staff a crew for a day nobody calls safe. Alaska knows exactly which days it's in danger. Somebody is finally paid to count the days it's allowed.
